title: F**K'ING MIDTERMS will COOK our Stocks...
speaker: Kevin Paffrath (Meet Kevin)

macro_themes.view: About 50 GW (~$3T) of data-center spending rests on local governments; midterm outcome sets the mandate.
Republican hold = higher-for-longer yields; Democratic sweep = most growth-positive; narrow Democratic House win = shutdown-style gridlock, worst case.
Slower capacity build boosts pricing power of big hyperscalers (MSFT, META, AMZN, GOOGL) at the expense of neoclouds.
Markets have historically gained in the 6-12 months after midterms; fine to be long on a low-risk basis.
Sees near-zero odds of a hike at the pre-midterm meeting unless the Oct 13 CPI is very bad.
Certain renewables (solar, wind, nuclear) win long-term regardless of political swings.

calls.reason: Yields stuck around his called peak of ~5.27%; 'rubber band fully stretched' and wants to snap back.
calls.quote: the rubber band is fully stretched, I feel like. Can you get a little bit more out of it? Sure. But it really wants to …

calls.reason: Bank of America data: gains in every 6-12 month period after midterms since WWII; S&P up 13% YTD vs typical 3% in midterm years.
calls.quote: it doesn't hurt to be long this market on sort of a low debt, lowrisk exposure basis.

calls.condition: Risk: data-center pushback/financing headwinds after a split-Congress midterm outcome.
calls.reason: Thinks Nebius is about to break out; neoclouds need anti-data-center sentiment to calm to finance growth.
calls.quote: companies like Nebus which I actually think is about to break out to 336.

notes: No on-air date; listing approx 2026-10-07 used. Content consistent with 2026-10-06 or 10-07 (10y 'ended at 52826' = 5.2826%). Recorded after the close. Most sector/ticker ideas are Morgan Stanley's (defense, financials, nuclear, data-center REITs, staples, CRWD/PANW/OKTA, Bloom, GE Vernova, hyperscalers) and are not recorded as his calls; he agrees on hyperscalers and cyber ('very expensive') without a stance. 'Nebus' = Nebius (NBIS); '336' target taken as-is. QQQ ~700 dip-buying is past, merged into ES. Considers a small Kalshi bet on a Republican sweep if odds fall to ~3%; not a market call.
